thread:
Lucy H.: Hey folks — I pushed a small draft to unify provisioning terminology and a short section with \"isolation heuristics\" that explains when tenants get moved to reserved pools vs preemptible hosts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123 :wave:
Raj Patel: Nice, this has been needed. Quick nit: 'isolation window' word sounds ambiguous. Maybe 'isolation lifecycle' or define it as a tuple (trigger, duration).
Lucy H.: Good point. I added a one-liner definition and an example timeline.
Maria G.: Can we include a tiny SDK snippet showing how to request 'isolation_preference' in the provisioning API? It'll help customer-facing examples.
Lucy H.: Added snippet in the PR under \"Examples -> SDK snippets\". Snippet is JS and Terraform.
Raj Patel: Quick review of the JS snippet: suggest using the async client pattern we recently standardized. Replace `client.createCapacity(...)` with `await client.capacity.create({...})` to match samples.
Lucy H.: Updated to async pattern. Also added a note about how isolation preference is advisory and that scale policies/priority still drive placement.
David S.: Heads up — SLA wording needs to call out that preemptible hosts can cause degraded latency for bursty requests. Suggest a short table mapping 'SLA tier' -> 'expected eviction behavior'.
docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123 (Lucy H.) — reviewers requested: @Raj Patel, @Maria G.
Maria G.: I added a Terraform snippet showing tenant labels + reserved_pool assignment. Snippet: ```hcl
resource \"redwood_capacity\" \"tenant\" {
  tenant_id = \"acme\"
  reserved_pool = \"silver-pools\"
  autoscale {
    target_qps = 120
    cooldown   = \"5m\"
  }
}
```
Raj Patel: tiny link fix: the section that references \"tenant eviction heuristics\" linked to the old internals doc. Point it at /docs/operational/eviction-behavior instead.
Lucy H.: Fixed link and left a comment to ask eng-runtime to confirm wording around quantized models impacting eviction latency.
David S.: Confirmed: quantized models can have slightly higher cold-start time on some hardware; added a short parenthetical in the heuristics section.
Maria G.: One more UX ask — call out the safe rollout pattern in the migration guide: 1) reserve small pool, 2) mirror traffic, 3) promote. Short bullets.
Lucy H.: Added the 3-step rollout bullets and an example CLI sequence. Example CLI: ```bash
redwoodctl capacity create --tenant acme --pool silver-pools --reserved
redwoodctl route mirror --from prod --to acme-staging
redwoodctl promote --pool acme-staging
```
eng-platform: Quick note from platform: please include the migration freeze window guidance when promoting to reserved pools (we recommend 15m quiet window).
Lucy H.: Added the freeze window note and a brief troubleshooting checklist for common failures (quota, tagging, KMS).
Raj Patel: LGTM from docs side. Maria, David — any objections before I tag for legal/SLAs?
Maria G.: No objections.
David S.: Fine by me.
Lucy H.: Thanks all — assigning reviewers and scheduling a tiny SIG-docs review tomorrow. :calendar:
